subject: Question - Adding letters/asterisks to denote statistical significance on graphs

messages.author: 9b666b3c6469b39f
messages.subject: Question - Adding letters/asterisks to denote statistical significance on graphs
parts:
Dear Davis R Users,

 

I wanted to know if there is available code/ R package that allows to add letters/asterisks to graphs denoting statistical significance (as calculated by a statistical test). See image attached showing what it would look like. Is there someone doing this using base graphics or ggplot?

 

Please let me know if you can help.

Thank you,

Marta

messages.author: 1ec981f6ad974842
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Question - Adding letters/asterisks to denote statistical significance on graphs
parts: If you're using ggplot2 and you only have a few bars to label, you could do this with geom_annotate().  See some examples here: http://docs.ggplot2.org/current/annotate.html

messages.author: f8f554f3c8aec296
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Question - Adding letters/asterisks to denote statistical significance on graphs
parts: The package lsmeans can calculate tukey groups and use compact letter display to plot them (in base graphics). You can also output the data underlying these groups as a data.frame which you can use to plot with ggplot. For doing that, annotate might work but also take a look at geom_label
